items.why: The report fits the 330-375 cm-1 band with two components: "2LA 351.09±0.05 (FWHM 8.94)" and "E' 355.29±0.06". It also shows that one Lorentzian leaves residual structure (rms 34 vs 12).

The fitted amplitudes imply 2LA/A1g of about 2.3 at spot 1 (1828 vs 806) and about 0.5 at spot 2 (540 vs 1134), but the report never states these ratios. It only quotes 2LA/E' ("about 4.3-4.9" vs "about 0.8") and says this "cannot be read as a thickness indicator", so it does not treat 2LA dominance as the monolayer fingerprint.
The A1g values match the rubric ("417.28" vs "420.08", a "+2.80 cm-1" shift). The interpretation is hedged to "monolayer or few-layer" and "thicker", not monolayer versus bulk-like.

The report gives "Delta(A1g-E2g) = 61.94±0.07 cm-1 in spot 1 and 64.66±0.04 cm-1 in spot 2", using the E' position from the two-component fit, and warns that 2LA "can bias the layer assignment if it is not fitted out."

The report says only vaguely that modes shift by "less than 3 cm-1" from mono- to few-layer and that spot 2's "N not determined". It never says that the steps between 2L, 3L and bulk are about 1 cm-1 and so weakly constrain N.

The report checks calibration against Si ("Si line positions differ by 0.12 cm-1 ... calibration offset cannot account for a 2.8 cm-1 A1 shift"). It also ties 2LA intensity to resonance at 514.5 nm (2.41 eV) near the A/B excitons.

wrong_claims.why: The report separates E' (355.3) from 2LA (351.1) and builds the separation on the separated E' position, not on the band maximum.
2LA(M) is identified as a resonant second-order overtone, and the report says "No defect-activated band is evident."
